correctness.rationale: For fixed B,y>0, f_{B,y}(z)=sin(pi B(z-iy))/(pi(z-iy)) has Fourier transform e^(2 pi y xi) on [-B/2,B/2], is in PW_{B/2}, and has genuine zeros a_n=n/B+iy. Set x=n/B. The unit-modulus multiplier splits as R_x(t)exp(2iyt/(x²+y²)) with R_x(t)-1=-2iyt/[conj(a)(a-t)]. For the t=x+s layer, x²|f(x+s)|² tends [sin²(pi Bs)+sinh²(pi By)]/pi² and m tends (s+iy)/(s-iy); integrating yields 2y/pi[cosh(2pi By)-exp(-2pi By)]. On the t=x²u scale away from zero, the oscillatory numerator averages to cosh(2pi By)/2 and the exponential contributes 2y/pi cosh(2pi By). Cutoff bounds rule out other order-x^-2 scales. Since Im⟨m f,f⟩=O(log x/x²), optimized phase changes squared distance only o(x^-2). Thus n² coefficient = B² times sum of two terms. Independently numerically evaluated both limiting integrals for three distinct (B,y), with finite truncation tolerances; these checks do not prove the two-scale convergence.
